newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt agrees to cut 1997 budget spending.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt agrees to cut 1997 budget spending.

text.p: The government, facing a vote of confidence in parliament this week, agreed on Monday to make unspecified cuts in 1997 budget spending, a spokesman said.

Talks on the extent of the cuts ministries would have to make were continuing, government spokesman Ivo Strejcek told reporters. He said the government had agreed an overall figure for the cuts, but declined to give details.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's three-party coalition had agreed on May 28 to make cuts as part of an austerity package.

Health Minister Jan Strasky earlier told the CTK news agency the government would propose cuts of just under 20 billion crowns. The government could face the confidence vote, which it called, as early as Tuesday.

Adoption of the austerity package was a condition for junior coalition partner, the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), supporting the government. Coalition parties control just 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house.

Leaders of the coalition agreed the austerity package, which included budget cuts and wage freezes, after two turbulent weeks in the foreign exchange markets that ended in the central bank floating the crown currency on May 27.
